condition_other: retinal degeneration / blindness (RCS blind rat model)
readout_other: visual cortex (VC) evoked potentials via tungsten needle electrode; light-evoked potentials for comparison
direction_notes: tFUS evoked VC potentials comparable to light-evoked responses; blind (RCS) rats showed significantly stronger responses than normal (LE) rats, and pulsed waveforms with PRF > 100 Hz additionally evoked long-duration low-frequency responses.

exposures.label: tFUS to visual cortex, continuous and pulsed waveform groups

timing.protocol_description: Three waveform groups were tested at the same amplitude: group 1, a single 15-ms continuous wave (CW) tone burst following a 6-s rest; group 2, two 2-ms CW tone bursts 20 ms apart, following a 6-s rest; group 3, pulsed waves with five PRF/pulse-width combinations (500 Hz/1 ms, 500 Hz/0.5 ms, 333.3 Hz/1 ms, 200 Hz/2 ms, 100 Hz/5 ms pulse), each delivered for 30 ms following a 6-s rest. During control recordings the transducer was aimed away from the brain with ultrasound still on.

source_quotes.n_subjects: 17 rats were studied. Six of them were normally sighted Long-Evan (LE) rats, and 11 were RD Royal College of Surgeon (RCS) blind rats.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: A self-designed 0.5-MHz transducer was used to stimulate the VC, with a center frequency of 0.5 MHz, 23-mm focal length, a f-number of 0.7 for a minimized focal area.
source_quotes.exposures[0].free_field.pressure_kpa: The measured focused ultrasound pressure in free field had a peak-to-peak amplitude of 3.74 MPa, the intensity I<sub>SPPA</sub> was 115.8 W/cm<sup>2</sup>, the mechanical index (MI) was 2.6.
source_quotes.exposures[0].free_field.isppa_w_cm2: The measured focused ultrasound pressure in free field had a peak-to-peak amplitude of 3.74 MPa, the intensity I<sub>SPPA</sub> was 115.8 W/cm<sup>2</sup>, the mechanical index (MI) was 2.6.

Five sets of parameters were used: 500-Hz PRF with 1-ms pulse, 500 Hz with 0.5-ms pulse, 333.3-Hz PRF with 1-ms pulse, 200-Hz PRF with 2-ms pulse, and 100-Hz PRF with 5-ms pulse. All stimulations were conducted for 30 ms following a rest of 6 s.

Five sets of parameters were used: 500-Hz PRF with 1-ms pulse, 500 Hz with 0.5-ms pulse, 333.3-Hz PRF with 1-ms pulse, 200-Hz PRF with 2-ms pulse, and 100-Hz PRF with 5-ms pulse. All stimulations were conducted for 30 ms following a rest of 6 s.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.duty_cycle_pct: (a) 1-ms pulse in every 2 ms (500 PRF and 50% DC). (b) 0.5-ms pulse in every 2 ms (500 PRF and 25% DC). (c) 1-ms pulse in every 3 ms (333.3 PRF and 33.3% DC). (d) 2-ms pulse in every 5 ms (200 PRF and 40% DC). (e) 5-ms pulse in every 10 ms (100 PRF and 50% DC).
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: 1) A 15-ms-long continuous wave (CW) following a rest of 6 s. 2) Two 2-ms-long CWs following a rest of 6 s. The interval between two waves was 20 ms. 3) Pulsed waves (PWs) with high pulse repetition frequency (PRF) were used in group 3. Five sets of parameters were used: 500-Hz PRF with 1-ms pulse, 500 Hz with 0.5-ms pulse, 333.3-Hz PRF with 1-ms pulse, 200-Hz PRF with 2-ms pulse, and 100-Hz PRF with 5-ms pulse. All stimulations were conducted for 30 ms following a rest of 6 s.

flags.reason: the single target/frequency exposure combines continuous-wave (groups 1-2: 15 ms and 2x2 ms tone bursts) and pulsed (group 3: five PRF/pulse-width combinations) sub-protocols, per the one-exposure-per-target-frequency rule; pulse_duration_ms/PRF/duty_cycle_pct lists reflect only the pulsed (group 3) sub-protocol, while sonication_duration_s lists durations from all three groups.
reported as a peak-to-peak amplitude (3.74 MPa), not a peak-negative or peak-positive pressure; recorded as stated.

the paper only estimates skull transmission loss qualitatively, citing an external reference for a 0.5-0.7 transmission factor to argue the mechanical index would remain within FDA limits after skull attenuation; no in-brain pressure/intensity value in kPa or W/cm2 is given by this study itself.
the paper describes a separate control experiment stimulating the auditory cortex directly (finding no VC response) rather than a standard masking/sham auditory control for the main experiment.
the paper describes one continuous recording procedure (baseline, light stimulation, ultrasound stimulation, control recording) per animal but never explicitly states a session count.
